newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy called up 3 to 5 cents on crop ratings.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy called up 3 to 5 cents on crop ratings.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were expected to open three to five cents higher Tuesday on disapointing weekly crop data, floor traders said.
Monday, USDA rated the U.S. soybean crop 57 percent good to excellent versus last week's rating of 55 percent.
A week of rains in dry areas in the central Midwest left many in the trade expecting soybean conditions to improve by as much as five percent.
Traders also characterized the markets as technically sound, which could also spur early buying, they said.
"Even with the rains, we couldn't break the market yesterday," said one commission house trader.
The ability of November to hold key support at $6.00 per bushel was viewed as a supportive factor for Tuesday, traders said.
In overnight Project A trade, soybeans 3/4 to 6-3/4 cents higher.
